title: Throwing a stoneware garlic keeper
subtitle: A lidded, ventilated stoneware jar that keeps fresh garlic cool and dry on the kitchen worktop
excerpt: A stoneware garlic keeper is a squat lidded jar with ventilation holes pierced in the body before bisque firing. The holes allow air circulation that prevents garlic from sweating and sprouting. This version is 100 mm tall, 95 mm in diameter, with a fitted domed lid. The lid requires a second throwing session.
sourceNotes: Stoneware garlic keeper throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage for piercing ventilation holes and trimming without distorting the form
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)
Pyrometric measure of heat-work in a kiln. Cone 6 approx 1220 degrees C

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.

A garlic keeper combines two separate thrown pieces , the body jar and the domed lid , fitted together at leather-hard using caliper measurements taken from the thrown rim. The ventilation holes are pierced at leather-hard before bisque. Leaving the outside of the lower body bare (unglazed) keeps the garlic cool and allows the clay's natural porosity to regulate humidity.

materials.name: Mid-fire glaze, pre-mixed
materials.quantity: inside of body and top of lid only

content.text: Wedge 600 g of grogged stoneware. Centre and open to a 60 mm floor. Pull walls to 100 mm height, flaring the form very slightly to 95 mm diameter at the rim.

At the rim, create a lid gallery (a slight inward step about 5 mm from the top, 5 mm wide) so the lid sits down into the opening rather than perching on top. Measure the gallery diameter with calipers and note it , this is the lid flange dimension.
Wire off and allow to dry to leather-hard.

, pierce a ring of 12 ventilation holes in the upper half of the body wall. Each hole should be 8 mm in diameter, spaced equally. Use the needle tool in a drilling motion. After piercing, smooth the inside edge of each hole lightly with a damp finger.

Wedge 250 g of the same clay. Throw a shallow dome , open a wide floor and collar the rim inward to create a dome shape 20 mm tall. The underside flange should match the lid gallery caliper dimension from the body.
Add a small knob: attach a 15 mm ball of clay to the top of the dome, score-and-slip, and press gently into a button shape.
fire body and lid together at

Glaze only the inside of the body and the top of the lid. Leave the outside body walls and the underside of the lid bare. Clean all glaze from foot-ring, base, and lid gallery. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Lid does not sit flush , too loose or too tight
rows.cause: Caliper measurement was taken before or after the leather-hard stage, not at the same moisture level for both pieces
rows.fix: Measure both body gallery and lid flange at the same leather-hard stage. Clay that is wetter than the gallery will be tighter once dry.

rows.cause: Piercing when the clay was still too soft distorted the wall; the stress concentrated at the hole edges and cracked
rows.fix: Pierce at true leather-hard only. If cracks appeared, fill with a small plug of same clay plus slip, smooth, and re-dry.
